questions.question: Which of the following is considered a defining feature of living organisms without any exception?
questions.explanation: Metabolism is a defining feature because all living organisms exhibit chemical reactions without exception.

questions.question: Consciousness is defined as awareness of surrounding environments. Which organism possesses 'self-consciousness'?
questions.explanation: Human being is the only organism who is aware of himself, possessing self-consciousness.

questions.question: According to binomial nomenclature, scientific names are written in which language and script?
options: Latin and printed in Normal text
questions.explanation: Biological names are generally in Latin and printed in italics.

questions.question: In the scientific name Mangifera indica Linn., what does 'Linn.' indicate?
questions.explanation: 'Linn.' indicates that the species was first described by Linnaeus.

questions.question: Which taxonomic category represents a collection of related families?
questions.explanation: Order is an assemblage of families exhibiting a few similar characters.

questions.question:
Statement I: Increase in mass and number are twin characteristics of growth.
Statement II: In plants, growth by cell division occurs continuously throughout life.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct facts from NCERT Biology.

questions.question:
Statement I: Reproduction cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic.
Statement II: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are living things.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement II is incorrect because in vitro metabolic reactions are living reactions, not living things.

questions.question:
Statement I: As we go higher from species to kingdom, common characteristics increase.
Statement II: Lower taxa share more characteristics.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Common characteristics decrease as we move from species to kingdom.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Non-living objects also grow if increase in mass is taken as a criterion.
Reason (R): Mass increases in non-living objects by accumulation of material on surface.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Mountains and boulders grow by extrinsic accumulation of material.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Scientific names are printed in italics.
Reason (R): Italics indicate their Latin origin.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Italics show Latin origin irrespective of the language.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Systematics takes into account evolutionary relationships.
Reason (R): Word systematics comes from Latin word 'systema'.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both are true NCERT facts, but origin of the word doesn't explain inclusion of phylogeny.

questions.question:
Match Column-I with Column-II:
Column-I: (A) Man (B) Housefly (C) Mango (D) Wheat
Column-II: (1) Sapindales (2) Poales (3) Primata (4) Diptera
questions.explanation: Man->Primata, Housefly->Diptera, Mango->Sapindales, Wheat->Poales.

questions.question:
Match Column-I with Column-II:
Column-I: (A) Family (B) Kingdom (C) Species (D) Genus
Column-II: (1) Highest category (2) Basic unit (3) Related species (4) Related genera
questions.explanation: Family->Group of related genera, Kingdom->Highest category, Species->Basic unit, Genus->Group of related species.

questions.question:
Match Column-I with Column-II:
Column-I: (A) Mango (B) Wheat (C) Housefly (D) Man
Column-II: (1) Muscidae (2) Hominidae (3) Anacardiaceae (4) Poaceae
questions.explanation: Mango->Anacardiaceae, Wheat->Poaceae, Housefly->Muscidae, Man->Hominidae.

questions.question: Which of the following represents ascending order of hierarchy?
options: Species -> Genus -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Phylum/Division -> Kingdom
Kingdom -> Phylum -> Class -> Order -> Family -> Genus -> Species
Species -> Family -> Genus -> Order -> Class -> Phylum -> Kingdom
Genus -> Species -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Division -> Kingdom
questions.explanation: Ascending order begins from species and ends at kingdom.

questions.question: Growth in unicellular organisms can be observed in vitro by:
options: Counting the number of cells under microscope
questions.explanation: In unicellular organisms, growth is easily observed in vitro cultures by simply counting the number of cells under a microscope.

questions.question: Growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events in:
options: Majority of higher animals and plants
questions.explanation: In majority of higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events.

questions.question: For unicellular organisms like Amoeba, growth is synonymous with:
questions.explanation: In unicellular organisms, increase in cell number represents both growth and reproduction simultaneously.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms multiply by fragmentation?
options: Fungi, filamentous algae, protonema of mosses
Mule, sterile worker bee, fertile human
questions.explanation: Fungi, filamentous algae, and protonema of mosses all easily multiply by fragmentation.

questions.question: True regeneration is observed in which of the following organisms?
questions.explanation: A fragmented organism regenerates the lost part of its body and becomes a new organism in Planaria.

questions.question: Which pair of organisms is non-reproducing?
questions.explanation: Mules, sterile worker bees, and infertile human couples do not reproduce.

questions.question: Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free systems. These isolated reactions are:
options: Neither living nor non-living, but living reactions
questions.explanation: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are not living things, but surely living reactions.

questions.question: The defining property of living organisms among the following is:
questions.explanation: Cellular organization, intrinsic growth, and consciousness are defining features without exception.

questions.question: What is the approximate estimated number of species known and described on Earth?
questions.explanation: The number of species that are known and described ranges between 1.7-1.8 million (biodiversity).

questions.question: ICBN stands for:
questions.explanation: ICBN stands for International Code for Botanical Nomenclature.

questions.question: ICZN stands for:
questions.explanation: ICZN stands for International Code of Zoological Nomenclature.

questions.question: Binomial Nomenclature was introduced by:
questions.explanation: Carolous Linnaeus developed and established Binomial Nomenclature.

questions.question: In a biological name, the first word represents ____ and the second component is ____.
questions.explanation: First word is Genus (starts with capital letter) and second word is specific epithet.

questions.question: When handwritten, scientific names are:
questions.explanation: Both words in a scientific name, when handwritten, are separately underlined.

questions.question: Taxonomy involves four basic processes. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: Basic processes of taxonomy are Characterisation, Identification, Classification, and Nomenclature.

questions.question: Which term includes characterisation, identification, nomenclature, classification, AND evolutionary relationships?
questions.explanation: Systematics takes into account evolutionary relationships between organisms.

questions.question: Taxonomic category is a part of overall taxonomic arrangement called:
questions.explanation: All taxonomic categories together constitute the taxonomic hierarchy.

questions.question: Each unit of classification is commonly termed as:
questions.explanation: Each category/rank represents a unit of classification termed as a taxon.

questions.question: Plural form of taxon is:
questions.explanation: Plural of taxon is taxa.

questions.question: Which of the following is the basic, lowest unit in taxonomic hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Taxonomic studies consider a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities as a species.

questions.question: Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Solanum nigrum share which common taxonomic rank?
questions.explanation: Both tuberosum and nigrum belong to the same genus Solanum.

questions.question: Panthera leo (lion), Panthera pardus (leopard), and Panthera tigris (tiger) belong to genus:
questions.explanation: Lion, leopard, and tiger are species belonging to genus Panthera.

questions.question: Cats belong to the genus:
questions.explanation: Cats are placed under genus Felis.

questions.question: Genus comprises a group of related:
questions.explanation: Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common than species of other genera.

questions.question: Plant families like Solanaceae and Convolvulaceae are included in order Polymoniales mainly based on:
questions.explanation: Plant families are included in the order Polymoniales mainly based on floral characteristics.

questions.question: Order Carnivora includes families like:
questions.explanation: Order Carnivora includes Felidae (cat family) and Canidae (dog family).

questions.question: Class Mammalia includes order Primata along with order:
questions.explanation: Class Mammalia includes order Primata (monkeys, apes, humans) and order Carnivora (tiger, cat, dog).

questions.question: Plants belonging to different classes with common characters like flowers and seeds are assigned to:
questions.explanation: For plants, classes with similar characters are assigned to a higher category called Division.

questions.question: In animal taxonomy, classes having dorsal hollow neural system and notochord are placed under Phylum:
questions.explanation: Presence of notochord and dorsal hollow neural system defines Phylum Chordata.

questions.question: Which of the following scientific names belongs to human beings?
questions.explanation: Human scientific name is Homo sapiens.

questions.question: Housefly belongs to which Phylum?
questions.explanation: Housefly (Musca domestica) belongs to Phylum Arthropoda.

questions.question: Wheat belongs to Class:
questions.explanation: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) is a monocot plant (Class Monocotyledonae).

questions.question: Mango belongs to Class:
questions.explanation: Mango (Mangifera indica) belongs to Class Dicotyledonae.

questions.question: Ernst Mayr is widely known as the:
questions.explanation: Ernst Mayr (1904–2004) was hailed as 'The Darwin of the 20th century'.

questions.question: Ernst Mayr was awarded which three prestigious prizes (The Balzan Prize, International Prize for Biology, Crafoord Prize) collectively called:
questions.explanation: Ernst Mayr was awarded the three prizes known as the triple crown of biology.

questions.question:
Statement I: All living organisms—past, present, and future—are linked to one another by sharing common genetic material.
Statement II: The genetic material is shared to varying degrees.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: All living organisms share common genetic material, but to varying degrees.

questions.question:
Statement I: In bacteria, growth and reproduction are synonymous.
Statement II: Bacteria reproduce exclusively by sexual methods.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement II is incorrect because bacteria mainly reproduce by cell division/fission (asexual).

questions.question:
Statement I: Plant growth is localized and indefinite.
Statement II: Animal growth is diffuse and definite.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Plants show continuous growth throughout life due to meristems; animal growth stops after a certain age.

questions.question:
Statement I: Solanum includes species like nigrum and melongena.
Statement II: Solanum, Panthera, and Felis are plant genera.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Panthera and Felis are animal genera, not plant genera.

questions.question:
Statement I: Dogs, cats, and mammals represent taxa at different levels.
Statement II: 'Taxa' can indicate categories at very different levels.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Taxa can designate categories at different levels (e.g., animals, mammals, dogs).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Photoperiod affects reproduction in seasonal breeders.
Reason (R): All organisms handle chemicals entering their bodies.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both are true statements from NCERT, but metabolism of chemicals doesn't explain photoperiodism.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Properties of tissues are not present in constituent cells.
Reason (R): Properties arise as a result of interactions among constituent cells.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Emergent properties of tissues arise due to interactions among constituent cells.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Properties of cellular organelles are present in molecular constituents.
Reason (R): Organelles are formed by interactions between molecular components.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Assertion is false because properties of organelles are NOT present in their molecular constituents.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Family Felidae includes both lions and cats.
Reason (R): Genus Panthera and genus Felis are placed under family Felidae.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Felidae contains both Panthera (lion) and Felis (cats).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Species is a group of individuals with fundamental similarities.
Reason (R): One species can be distinguished from another based on distinct morphological differences.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Distinct morphological differences allow separation of closely related species.

questions.question:
Match Column-I (Organism) with Column-II (Genus):
Column-I: (A) Mango (B) Wheat (C) Housefly (D) Human
Column-II: (1) Homo (2) Musca (3) Mangifera (4) Triticum
questions.explanation: Mango->Mangifera, Wheat->Triticum, Housefly->Musca, Human->Homo.

questions.question:
Match Column-I (Organism) with Column-II (Class):
Column-I: (A) Human (B) Housefly (C) Mango (D) Wheat
Column-II: (1) Insecta (2) Mammalia (3) Monocotyledonae (4) Dicotyledonae
questions.explanation: Human->Mammalia, Housefly->Insecta, Mango->Dicotyledonae, Wheat->Monocotyledonae.

questions.question:
Match Column-I with Column-II:
Column-I: (A) Binomial nomenclature (B) Systema Naturae (C) Triple crown of biology (D) Defining feature
Column-II: (1) Linnaeus book (2) Ernst Mayr (3) Consciousness (4) Linnaeus rule
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature rule by Linnaeus, Systema Naturae is Linnaeus's publication, Triple crown = Mayr, Defining feature = Consciousness.

questions.question: Self-consciousness is the characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Only humans possess self-consciousness.

questions.question: In binomial nomenclature, the species epithet starts with a:
questions.explanation: Specific epithet starts with a small letter.

questions.question: In binomial nomenclature, the generic name starts with a:
questions.explanation: Generic name starts with a capital letter.

questions.question: Biological names are derived from which language, irrespective of origin?
questions.explanation: Biological names are Latinised or derived from Latin.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of all living things?
questions.explanation: Extrinsic growth (accumulation from outside) is a feature of non-living objects.

questions.question: A patient in coma lies in a hospital supported by machines. He has no self-consciousness. Such a patient is:
questions.explanation: NCERT mentions coma patients are brain dead with no self-consciousness.

questions.question: Sum total of all chemical reactions occurring in our body is called:
questions.explanation: Sum total of chemical reactions = Metabolism.

questions.question: The process by which anything is grouped into convenient categories based on easily observable characters is:
questions.explanation: Classification is grouping based on observable characters.

questions.question: Scientific term for categories at different levels is:
questions.explanation: Scientific term for these categories is taxa.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to family Muscidae?
questions.explanation: Housefly belongs to Muscidae family.

questions.question: Which family does wheat belong to?
questions.explanation: Wheat belongs to family Poaceae.

questions.question: Which family does mango belong to?
questions.explanation: Mango belongs to family Anacardiaceae.

questions.question: Which order does mango belong to?
questions.explanation: Mango belongs to order Sapindales.

questions.question: Which order does wheat belong to?
questions.explanation: Wheat belongs to order Poales.

questions.question: Order Carnivora is placed in Class:
questions.explanation: Order Carnivora belongs to Class Mammalia.

questions.question: Phylum Arthropoda includes animals characterized by:
questions.explanation: Jointed appendages are characteristic of Arthropoda.

questions.question: In plants, highest taxonomic category is:
questions.explanation: Kingdom is the highest category for both plants and animals.

questions.question:
Statement I: Nomenclature is only possible when the organism is described correctly.
Statement II: Identification is determining whether an un-named organism is same as a known one.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements correctly define identification and prerequisite for nomenclature.

questions.question:
Statement I: Non-living objects exhibit metabolism.
Statement II: No non-living object exhibits metabolism.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Metabolism is totally absent in non-living objects.

questions.question:
Statement I: All prokaryotes can sense and respond to environmental cues.
Statement II: Most complex eukaryotes can sense and respond to environmental cues.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: All organisms from simple prokaryotes to complex eukaryotes show consciousness.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Classification is not a single step process.
Reason (R): It involves hierarchy of steps in which each step represents a rank or category.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Classification involves hierarchy of steps, so it is not a single-step process.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Dog, Mammals, and Animals represent different taxa.
Reason (R): Taxa can indicate categories at very different levels.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Dog is a species/genus level taxon, Mammal is class, Animal is kingdom.

questions.question:
Match Column-I with Column-II:
Column-I: (A) Triticum aestivum (B) Mangifera indica (C) Homo sapiens (D) Musca domestica
Column-II: (1) Diptera (2) Primata (3) Sapindales (4) Poales
questions.explanation: Triticum->Poales, Mangifera->Sapindales, Homo->Primata, Musca->Diptera.

questions.question: Systema Naturae was written by:
questions.explanation: Linnaeus published Systema Naturae.

questions.question: Word 'Systematics' is derived from Latin word 'Systema' which means:
questions.explanation: Systema means systematic arrangement of organisms.

questions.question: Genera Solanum, Petunia, and Datura are placed in family:
questions.explanation: Solanum, Petunia, and Datura belong to family Solanaceae.

questions.question: Human beings belong to family:
questions.explanation: Humans belong to family Hominidae.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an animal family?
questions.explanation: Anacardiaceae is a plant family (Mango).

questions.question: Organisms that can respond to environmental stimuli are:
questions.explanation: Both prokaryotes and eukaryotes show consciousness.

questions.question: The phenomenon of Photoperiodism regulates reproduction in:
questions.explanation: Photoperiod affects reproduction in seasonal breeders, both plants and animals.

questions.question: In majority of higher plants and animals, growth and reproduction are:
questions.explanation: They are mutually exclusive in higher organisms.

questions.question: Cell division occurs in animals up to a certain age, but cell division occurs in plant tissues:
questions.explanation: Plants grow continuously throughout their life by cell division.

questions.question: Which feature is common to Fungi, Filamentous Algae, and Protonema of mosses?
questions.explanation: All three easily multiply by fragmentation.

questions.question: Dead organisms do not show:
questions.explanation: Dead organisms show none of these defining living characteristics.

questions.question: Modern taxonomic studies utilize information from:
questions.explanation: Modern taxonomy relies on external/internal structure, cell structure, development, and ecology.

questions.question: First step in taxonomy is:
questions.explanation: Characterisation and identification come first.

questions.question: Biological name of Mango is:
questions.explanation: Mangifera indica is the scientific name of Mango.

questions.question: Biological name of Wheat is:
questions.explanation: Triticum aestivum is wheat.

questions.question: Biological name of Housefly is:
questions.explanation: Housefly is Musca domestica.

questions.question:
Statement I: Genus Solanum includes potato and brinjal.
Statement II: Genus Panthera includes lion, leopard, and tiger.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct examples of genus from NCERT.

questions.question:
Statement I: Families are characterized on the basis of both vegetative and reproductive features of plant species.
Statement II: Solanaceae is a plant family.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Families are defined by vegetative and reproductive floral characters.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Lower the taxon, more are the characteristics that members share.
Reason (R): Higher the category, greater is the difficulty of determining relationship to other taxa at same level.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both are correct facts, but difficulty in determination at higher level does not explain character sharing at lower level.

questions.question: Which of the following is an incorrect combination?
questions.explanation: Man belongs to Order Primata, not Carnivora.

questions.question: Which of the following is an incorrect combination?
questions.explanation: Housefly belongs to Family Muscidae, not Felidae.

questions.question: Which taxon is common to both Mango and Wheat?
questions.explanation: Both belong to Kingdom Plantae / Division Angiospermae.

questions.question: The name of author appears after the:
questions.explanation: Author's name appears after specific epithet e.g., Mangifera indica Linn.

questions.question: Binomial name of potato is:
questions.explanation: Solanum tuberosum is potato.

questions.question: Brinjal belongs to specific epithet:
questions.explanation: Solanum melongena is brinjal.

questions.question: Makoi belongs to specific epithet:
questions.explanation: Solanum nigrum is Makoi.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a group of related genera?
questions.explanation: Family has a group of related genera.

questions.question: Which of the following represents an assemblage of families?
questions.explanation: Order is an assemblage of families.

questions.question: Which of the following includes related orders?
questions.explanation: Class includes related orders.

questions.question: Which category includes related classes in animals?
questions.explanation: Phylum includes related classes in animals.

questions.question: In plants, equivalent level to Phylum is:
questions.explanation: Division is used for plants instead of Phylum.

questions.question: Highest taxonomic category in animal classification is:
questions.explanation: Kingdom Animalia is the highest category.

questions.question: Which feature is NOT shared by non-living objects?
questions.explanation: Non-living objects show none of these features.

questions.question: Increase in mass in non-living objects is by:
questions.explanation: Non-living growth is extrinsic via accumulation on surface.

questions.question: Growth in living organisms is:
questions.explanation: Living growth comes from inside (intrinsic).

questions.question: Reproduction is not defining because:
options: Some living organisms do not reproduce
questions.explanation: Mules and worker bees do not reproduce, so it cannot be defining.

questions.question: Metabolism is defining because:
options: Isolated reactions in vitro are living reactions
questions.explanation: Metabolism is present in all living forms and absent in non-living objects.

questions.question: The process of naming living organisms is:
questions.explanation: Nomenclature is standardizing the name of an organism.

questions.question: The process of identifying an organism's position in classification is:
questions.explanation: Identification is determining correct placement based on characteristics.

questions.question: In Mangifera indica, 'Mangifera' represents:
questions.explanation: Mangifera is the genus.

questions.question: In Mangifera indica, 'indica' represents:
questions.explanation: indica is the specific epithet.

questions.question: The generic name Panthera includes:
questions.explanation: Panthera leo, Panthera pardus, and Panthera tigris.

questions.question: Dog belongs to family:
questions.explanation: Dogs belong to Canidae family.

questions.question: Cats belong to family:
questions.explanation: Cats belong to Felidae family.

questions.question: Order Carnivora is characterized by inclusion of:
questions.explanation: Carnivora includes cat and dog families.

questions.question: Order Primata includes:
questions.explanation: Primata includes monkeys, apes, and humans.

questions.question: Monocotyledonae and Dicotyledonae are:
questions.explanation: They are classes under Division Angiospermae.

questions.question: Insecta is a:
questions.explanation: Insecta is a class of Phylum Arthropoda.

questions.question: Diptera is an:
questions.explanation: Diptera is the order of housefly.

questions.question: Sapindales is an:
questions.explanation: Sapindales is the order of mango.

questions.question: Poales is an:
questions.explanation: Poales is the order of wheat.

questions.question:
Statement I: Scientific names ensure that each organism has only one name.

options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct

questions.question:

A is true but R is false

questions.question: The total diversity of life on earth is called:

questions.question: Which category has the minimum number of common characters?
questions.explanation: Highest rank (Kingdom) has minimum shared characters.

questions.question: The term 'Systematics' deals with:

Identification and naming of plants only

questions.question: Taxonomic hierarchy refers to:
options: Step-wise arrangement of all categories for classification of plants and animals
questions.explanation: Hierarchy is the stepwise arrangement of categories.

questions.question: Datura belongs to family:

questions.question: Petunia belongs to family:

questions.question: Polymoniales includes families based on:

questions.question: Mammalia is characterized by presence of:

questions.question: Division Angiospermae includes plants that have:

questions.question: Chordata includes animals with:
options: Notochord and dorsal hollow nerve cord

questions.question:
Statement I: Human scientific name is written as Homo sapiens Linn.

options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Homo sapiens Linn. shows author name at the end.

questions.question:
Statement I: Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae belong to order Polymoniales.
Statement II: Felidae and Canidae belong to order Carnivora.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Both order classifications are NCERT statements.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): All living organisms show metabolism.
Reason (R): Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated in cell-free systems.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: In vitro demonstration does not explain why living organisms show metabolism.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a taxon?
questions.explanation: Dogs, Mammals, Plants are taxa; rank concept itself is an abstract category.

questions.question: Binomial name of Housefly in correct format is:
questions.explanation: Generic name capitalized, specific epithet small, italicized.

questions.question: Scientific name of Wheat in correct format is:
questions.explanation: Triticum aestivum in italics.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct regarding Linnaeus?
questions.explanation: Linnaeus contributed all of these.

questions.question: Growth cannot be taken as defining feature of living organisms because:
options: Non-living objects also grow by accumulation
Some living organisms do not grow
questions.explanation: Extrinsic growth in non-living objects prevents growth from being defining.

questions.question: Reproduction cannot be an all-inclusive defining feature because:
options: There are many living organisms which do not reproduce
Reproduction is absent in lower plants
questions.explanation: Sterile organisms like worker bees, mules, infertile couples do not reproduce.

questions.question: Defining features of living organisms are:
questions.explanation: Metabolism, Cellular Organization, and Consciousness have no exceptions.

questions.question: Unicellular organisms reproduce by:
questions.explanation: Cell division is the primary method of reproduction in unicellular organisms.

questions.question: Amoeba reproduces by cell division. In Amoeba, growth and reproduction are:
questions.explanation: In Amoeba, growth and reproduction mean cell division (synonymous).

questions.question: Regeneration of lost body part into complete organism is seen in:
questions.explanation: Planaria shows true regeneration.

questions.question: Fungi reproduce sexually and asexually. Millions of asexual spores are produced in fungi for reproduction. Protonema of moss multiplies by:
questions.explanation: Protonema of mosses multiplies by fragmentation.

questions.question: In living organisms, growth is from:
questions.explanation: Living growth is intrinsic.

questions.question: Which statement is true for metabolic reactions?
options: They occur in all living organisms without exception
They can be performed in test tubes
In vitro reactions are non-living reactions
questions.explanation: Metabolism occurs in all living forms and isolated reactions can be run in test tubes.

questions.question: All living organisms are aware of their surroundings. This property is:
questions.explanation: Awareness of surroundings is consciousness.

questions.question: Which organism responds to photoperiod for breeding?
questions.explanation: Seasonal breeders respond to photoperiod.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct sequence of taxonomic basic processes?
questions.explanation: Characterization precedes identification, then classification and nomenclature.

questions.question: Earliest classifications were based on the 'uses' of various organisms because:
options: Basic needs of food, clothing, and shelter
questions.explanation: Human beings needed to use organisms for food, clothing, and shelter.

questions.question: The term 'Taxon' represents:
options: A unit of classification at any level
questions.explanation: Taxon can represent any rank in hierarchy.

questions.question: Which of the following is a taxon?
questions.explanation: Dicotyledonae is a specific taxon; class, order, phylum are abstract categories.

questions.question: Which of the following is a category?
questions.explanation: Class is a category; others are taxa.

questions.question: Find the odd one out with respect to taxonomic rank:
questions.explanation: Chordata is a Phylum; Mammalia, Insecta, and Dicotyledonae are Classes.

questions.question: Group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities is called:
questions.explanation: Species is defined as group of individuals with fundamental similarities.

questions.question: Potato and brinjal belong to:
questions.explanation: Both are in genus Solanum.

questions.question: Lion, Leopard, and Tiger belong to genus Panthera. They differ in their:
questions.explanation: Panthera leo, Panthera pardus, Panthera tigris differ in specific epithets.

questions.question: Genus Felis includes:
questions.explanation: Genus Felis includes cats.

questions.question: Solanaceae family includes genera like:
questions.explanation: Solanum, Petunia, and Datura belong to Solanaceae.

questions.question: Which of the following characters are mainly used to classify plant families into orders?
questions.explanation: Floral characters determine plant orders like Polymoniales.

questions.question: Order Carnivora includes families:
questions.explanation: Felidae (cats) and Canidae (dogs).

questions.question: Class Mammalia includes order Primata and order Carnivora. Primata includes:
questions.explanation: Primata includes monkey, gorilla, gibbon, human.

questions.question: Classes with similar characters like presence of dorsal hollow neural system belong to phylum:
questions.explanation: Phylum Chordata.

questions.question: Plant classes with few similar characters are assigned to higher category called:
questions.explanation: Division is used for plants.

questions.question: Kingdom Animalia includes all animals belonging to various:
questions.explanation: Animals of various phyla belong to Kingdom Animalia.

questions.question: Kingdom Plantae includes all plants from various:
questions.explanation: Plants of various divisions belong to Kingdom Plantae.

questions.question:
Statement I: As we go higher from species to kingdom, number of common characteristics decreases.
Statement II: Lower the category, higher is the number of common features.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements describe taxonomic hierarchy rules accurately.

questions.question:
Statement I: Scientific name of housefly is Musca domestica.
Statement II: Housefly belongs to class Insecta and phylum Arthropoda.
options: Both Statement I and II are correct
Both Statement I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are facts from NCERT table 1.1.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Determination of relationship becomes complex at kingdom level.
Reason (R): Number of common characteristics is lowest at kingdom level.
options: Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Fewer common characters at higher levels make determining relationships more complex.

questions.question:
Match Column-I (Taxon) with Column-II (Rank for Housefly):
Column-I: (A) Musca (B) Muscidae (C) Diptera (D) Insecta
Column-II: (1) Class (2) Order (3) Family (4) Genus
questions.explanation: Musca->Genus, Muscidae->Family, Diptera->Order, Insecta->Class.

questions.question:
Match Column-I (Taxon) with Column-II (Rank for Wheat):
Column-I: (A) Triticum (B) Poaceae (C) Poales (D) Monocotyledonae
Column-II: (1) Class (2) Order (3) Family (4) Genus
questions.explanation: Triticum->Genus, Poaceae->Family, Poales->Order, Monocotyledonae->Class.

questions.question:
Match Column-I (Taxon) with Column-II (Rank for Mango):
Column-I: (A) Mangifera (B) Anacardiaceae (C) Sapindales (D) Dicotyledonae
Column-II: (1) Class (2) Order (3) Family (4) Genus
questions.explanation: Mangifera->Genus, Anacardiaceae->Family, Sapindales->Order, Dicotyledonae->Class.

questions.question:
Match Column-I (Taxon) with Column-II (Rank for Human):
Column-I: (A) Homo (B) Hominidae (C) Primata (D) Mammalia
Column-II: (1) Class (2) Order (3) Family (4) Genus
questions.explanation: Homo->Genus, Hominidae->Family, Primata->Order, Mammalia->Class.

questions.question: Biological classification helps in:
options: Organizing huge biodiversity into systematic categories
questions.explanation: All are primary objectives of biological classification.

questions.question: Ernst Mayr served as professor at which university?
questions.explanation: Ernst Mayr was Alexander Agassiz Professor of Zoology Emeritus at Harvard University.

questions.question: Ernst Mayr pioneered the currently accepted definition of:
questions.explanation: Mayr defined biological species concept (interbreeding natural population).

questions.question: Which process is NOT essential for taxonomic study?
questions.explanation: Local language naming leads to confusion and is not part of scientific taxonomy.

questions.question: Family of Mango is Anacardiaceae. Family ends generally with suffix '-aceae' in:
questions.explanation: Plant families end with the suffix -aceae.

questions.question: Order of Wheat is Poales. Plant orders generally end with suffix:
questions.explanation: Plant orders usually end with -ales.

questions.question: The complete taxonomic position of Human is:
options: Homo sapiens, Genus: Homo, Family: Hominidae, Order: Primata, Class: Mammalia, Phylum: Chordata
Homo sapiens, Genus: Homo, Family: Felidae, Order: Carnivora, Class: Mammalia
Homo sapiens, Genus: Sapiens, Family: Homo, Order: Primata
Homo sapiens, Genus: Homo, Family: Muscidae, Order: Diptera
questions.explanation: Complete hierarchy for humans according to NCERT.
